material_caveats: The frozen selection rule used the full development sample; its internal confirmation slice is descriptive, not independent out-of-sample evidence. The sealed year is the independent test.
Crude oil supplied most sealed profit; the yen sleeve was nearly flat. This is a three-rule portfolio, not broad diversification.
The ten best days account for essentially all sealed profit, although the portfolio remains strong after removing the best day and profitable after removing the best five days.
Sealed volatility rose to 18.2% versus the 10% development target because leverage was frozen rather than dynamically refit.
Costs are modeled as 1 bp per side. Development stress remained at 2.22 Sharpe at 3.5 bps per side, but live fills, margin, exchange fees, and market impact require broker-specific validation.

Local continuous-series files do not contain trustworthy contract identifiers. The strategy therefore avoids overnight exposure and uses only same-session open-to-close returns, but a contract-level execution study remains required before live deployment.
The S&P comparison uses the FRED daily S&P 500 price index and excludes dividends; the strategy result is also hypothetical and excludes financing and taxes.
decision: The candidate passes the requested research audit and sealed Sharpe target. It is suitable for paper trading and contract-level execution validation, not immediate capital deployment.
